boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten campus and campus-adjacent places with documented uses for studying, meeting, recreation, and taking a break between classes.

cards.title: Build a Study Session Around Roux Library
cards.subtitle: Carrels, computers, group areas, meeting rooms, and casual seating
cards.notes: Choose a carrel for focused work or move to a group area when conversation helps; ask the circulation desk about loanable study supplies.
cards.short_summary: A flexible academic base with hundreds of seats arranged for individual, group, and casual work.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Southern states that Roux Library supports student scholarship and provides carrel and computer seating, group-study areas, meeting rooms, casual seats, and café seating.
cards.access_notes: In-house resources are available to the public, but facility and service priority is reserved for Florida Southern students, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Pair Computer Work With a Café Break
cards.subtitle: A late-opening student-computing option inside Roux Library
cards.notes: Bring work that benefits from a computer, then use the café setting for a less formal session; confirm library access before arriving.
cards.short_summary: Library-based computing and café seating make this a practical change of pace from a conventional study floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Southern identifies Tûtû’s Cyber Café inside Roux Library as a student-computing option with coffee, lunch, and snack service.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Roux Library. The official page says it opens late most evenings but does not provide a current daily schedule; verify before visiting.

cards.title: Try an Archives Carrel for Solo Work
cards.subtitle: Four private study carrels on the second floor
cards.notes: Use a second-floor carrel when you need a one-person workspace; arrive with a backup plan because the rooms are first-come, first-served.
cards.short_summary: The archives building offers a small set of private carrels beyond the library’s main study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Southern says students, staff, and faculty may use four private study carrels on the second floor of the McKay Archives Center.
cards.access_notes: Carrels are for one person and available first-come, first-served. College borrowing privileges require a valid FSC ID.

cards.title: Meet Inside a Wright-Era Reading Room
cards.subtitle: A renovated gathering room in the Thaddeus G. Buckner Building
cards.notes: Look for scheduled organization meetings or lectures here, and notice the surviving tiered desks from the building’s original library use.
cards.short_summary: A former library reading room now documented as a venue for campus organizations, lectures, and special proceedings.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Southern’s archives document that the Hollis Room became a meeting place for organizations such as Student Government Association and for lectures.
cards.source_title: History of the Thaddeus G. Buckner Building
cards.access_notes: Use depends on scheduled campus activities and building access; the source does not state unrestricted drop-in availability.

cards.title: Use the Wellness Center as a Recreation Hub
cards.subtitle: Fitness equipment, classes, courts, and student recreation services
cards.notes: Bring your current FSC ID, check the posted schedule, and choose among fitness equipment, court sports, or an organized exercise class.
cards.short_summary: The central access point for indoor fitness, recreation programming, and equipment-based activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Southern identifies the Hollis Wellness Center as its home for fitness, wellness, and recreation, with access for current students using an ID card.
cards.access_notes: Current FSC students access the facilities with a current ID card. Hours and closures vary, so consult the Office of Wellness schedule first.

cards.title: Switch From Laps to the Recreation Shallow End
cards.subtitle: An eight-lane pool with space for water games and relaxed swimming
cards.notes: Check pool hours before walking over, bring required swim gear, and use only provided equipment according to lifeguard and facility rules.
cards.short_summary: A competition pool that also supports recreational swimming, water basketball, and volleyball.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Southern describes an eight-lane, 25-yard competition pool with an attached shallow recreation area and equipment for water activities.
cards.access_notes: Pool hours may change for breaks, holidays, maintenance, or team use. Follow lifeguard instructions and posted aquatic policies.

cards.title: Launch a Paddle Session From MocDock
cards.subtitle: The student waterfront base on Lake Hollingsworth
cards.notes: Bring your FSC ID, sign the waiver, wear the supplied lifejacket throughout the outing, and follow every direction from the waterfront attendant.
cards.short_summary: A staffed waterfront base where students can check out kayaks and paddleboards during the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Southern says the MocDock waterfront program is free for students, faculty, and staff and provides kayak and paddleboard checkout with an FSC ID and waiver.
cards.access_notes: Open Friday through Sunday during the academic year and closed during the posted summer period. FSC ID, waiver, lifejacket, and attendant compliance are required.

cards.title: Bring a Group to the Intramural Fields
cards.subtitle: Callahan Court fields used for Ultimate Frisbee and flag football
cards.notes: Check programming or field availability before organizing a game, then borrow eligible sports equipment from the Wellness Center if needed.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor fields give informal groups and intramural programs room for field sports.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Southern identifies its Intramural Fields on Callahan Court as spaces used for sports including Ultimate Frisbee and flag football.
cards.access_notes: Field availability may be affected by intramural schedules, reservations, weather, and campus operations; verify before planning a group game.

cards.title: Set Up a Sand-Volleyball Break
cards.subtitle: Courts on Columbia Street across from Wynee’s Bistro
cards.notes: Gather enough players, check whether the courts are scheduled, and ask the Wellness Center about borrowing a volleyball before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor court area suited to a quick pickup game between other campus commitments.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Southern states that it maintains sand volleyball courts on Columbia Street across from Wynee’s Bistro and offers sports-equipment checkout.
cards.access_notes: Confirm court availability and equipment-checkout requirements with the Wellness Center; organized programming may take priority.

cards.entity_name: Ashley Gibson Barnett Museum of Art
cards.title: Use the Museum for an Art Reset
cards.subtitle: A Florida Southern cultural center two blocks north of campus
cards.notes: Check the current exhibitions before leaving campus, then use a short gallery visit as a visual break or starting point for creative coursework.
cards.short_summary: A campus-adjacent museum gives students a documented, no-admission-cost place to engage with changing exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida Southern’s October 2025 parent newsletter states that the campus-adjacent Ashley Gibson Barnett Museum of Art provides free admission to all, including students.
cards.access_notes: Located two blocks north of the College. Check the museum’s current opening schedule and exhibition notices before visiting.
